text:
Priya: Hey team — ran into a reproducible race during vram-lease reconciliation when a tenant process detaches and immediately re-attaches under heavy concurrency. Repro steps + logs below. Looking for quick ideas and whether we should do a small API refactor or just a hotfix.

Priya: Repro: spin 200 small inference requests while restarting tenant agent; sometimes we see leaked leases and then a double-free attempt on host-staging buffer.

Priya: Example log snippet:
``
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] lease_manager: revoke(lease_id=0x7f12ef) triggered by detach
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] staging_pool: free_async(addr=0x7ffcc000)
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] reconcile: tenant_reclaim start(tenant=acct-123)
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] reconcile: observed lease still referenced in in-flight-kvcache
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] error: double free detected in host proxy
```

Ben: ugh. iirc we only do a best-effort walk of in-flight kvcache refs during reconcile. if detach->reattach happens quick, reconcile can believe leases are unused and free them while the old request still has a ref. we should either make reconcile wait for quiescence or convert free_async to a deferred-ownership swap.

Anna: Agree. Two quick options:
1) conservative: reconcile waits for in-flight counter to hit zero (or a short grace window). simpler but increases tail latency during churn.
2) aggressive: reconcile marks leases "revoked" and moves ownership to a pending-retire list; actual free happens after explicit ack from the request lifecycle. More complex but removes pause.

Miguel: tradeoffs: (1) is simpler and less API churn but has scaling problems if many tenants churn frequently. (2) needs lifecycle hooks in request path -> adds per-token path cost unless we batch acks.

Priya: my PoC tried (2) with a pending-retire queue and a small epoch number. sketch:
```
- on detach: mark leases REVOKED and enqueue to retireq
- request completion: if lease.state == REVOKED -> decrement retire refcount and maybe trigger free
- background janitor flushes retireq every 50ms
```
Patch size ~120 LOC. reduced double-free runs in my stress harness.

Ben: curious — did you also consider using an RCU-ish grace period where we bump a global epoch on detach and requests advance their local epoch? that avoids per-request checks but needs epoch advancement semantics.

Priya: I tried epoch too. RCU path lowered per-request cost but introduced complexity on multi-worker request scheduling and made debugging harder when epochs got out of sync. Also harder to port to the private deploy w/ constrained kernels.

Anna: API boundary question: if we add a REVOKED state and require request path to check it, that's a contract change between runtime and request worker. We should keep it optional behind a feature flag for Dedicated/Hosted until we stabilize.

Miguel: Also think about QoS: batches that reattach fast could congest retireq causing memory spikes. Need backpressure — maybe bound retireq with eviction policy: if retireq > threshold, fall back to blocking reconcile for that tenant.

Ben: another possibility: piggyback lease ownership on the KVHandle itself — when kvcache holds a handle, it pins the lease. Reconcile would only free leases without any pins. That moves logic into kvcache which already tracks handles.

Priya: that's promising — minimal request path cost, centralizes logic. But requires kvcache->lease coupling; need to define small API: kvcache.pin_lease(lease_id) / unpin_lease(lease_id). Backwards compatibility: old handles return noop pins.

Anna: If we go kvcache-pin, we'll need to audit existing callsites (rerank, embedding hot paths). We should also add metrics: pinned_lease_count, retireq_depth, reconcile_block_count.

Miguel: ops concern: in private/onprem some customers have NVME-backed staging pools with slower free. The retireq could accumulate. We should add a per-tenant memory-watermark and a forced-block if free cannot keep up.

Priya: Proposed incremental plan:
- short-term hotfix: add a 50ms quiescence window before reconcile frees leases (config flag off by default) -> low risk
- medium: implement kvcache.pin_lease API and migrate request holders (low per-request cost)
- long-term: replace retireq with pin-based lifecycle and optional epoch mode for specific perf-critical hosts

Ben: +1. Hotfix first to stop customer-impact.

Anna: I'll draft a small RFC for kvcache-pin API; include API compatibility notes and migration plan. Assign to Priya and Ben for PoC.

Miguel: I'll sketch the ops guardrails (per-tenant watermark + alerting). Also add a stress test that simulates detach->reattach churn with NVME slowness.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/lease-hotfix -> eng-runtime at 2026-03-12T09:00:00Z

Priya: Thanks all. I'll open the PR with hotfix flagged behind rollout config, attach the stress harness, and link RFC draft once Anna starts it. Follow-up: assign reviewers @Ben @Anna. :thumbsup:
